source.title: Block-diagonal Hessian-free Optimization for Training Neural Networks
source.authors: Hui-Shuai Zhang; Caiming Xiong; James Bradbury; R. Socher

record.tranche_reason: Compares held-out performance across batch sizes and optimization methods, but does not use a fixed epoch budget or directly measure the train-test gap as V5 describes.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior large-batch generalization results in its introduction; those cited results are not extracted. Its own comparisons report held-out performance for MNIST classification and CIFAR-10 classification, with some outcomes described only in figures.
record.test_reason: The study uses the reported large-batch generalization problem to motivate its optimizer and reports its own method's performance. Its comparisons change optimizer and batch size together and stop at declining test accuracy or 1000 epochs, rather than comparing held-out performance at a fixed epoch budget. They do not establish V5's batch-size penalty or its removal. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that block-diagonal HF improves convergence and stability over ordinary HF and scales better to large batches than Adam, requiring roughly an order of magnitude fewer updates. Held-out performance is better on sequential MNIST and comparable to small-batch Adam on CIFAR-10. Fewer updates do not establish proportional runtime savings: HF updates cost 5–10 times as much as Adam updates.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes block-diagonal Hessian-free optimization and compares it with ordinary Hessian-free and Adam; it does not reproduce the original large-batch training recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Held-out performance is compared across optimization methods and batch sizes; the CNN comparison uses Polyak averaging for all three algorithms.

fits_no_version.finding: Large-batch block-diagonal HF reaches better sequential-MNIST test accuracy than the tested Adam settings and comparable CIFAR-10 test accuracy to small-batch Adam, with fewer parameter updates under the study's stopping rule.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Block-diagonal Hessian-free optimization can achieve competitive held-out performance with large batches and fewer updates than Adam in these experiments.

record.peer_reviewed: under review as a conference paper at ICLR 2018
record.problems: The paper does not report numeric held-out metrics in the text for these comparisons; the relevant plots are figure-based. It does not hold epoch budgets fixed, and it does not directly report train-test gaps.
record.rows_left_out: No separately described numeric batch-size result was recoverable from the supplied flattened figure text; cited results from other studies were excluded.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD under the specified tuning conditions; HF versus Adam does not test this comparison.
The large-batch penalty under fixed epoch budgets and whether recipe adaptations remove that penalty; language-model results.
Effects of adding or removing dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, generalization gaps, and ranking against alternative measures.
Accuracy after removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied flattened figures do not permit reliable numerical accuracy extraction. A train–test gap is not required to test V5; the decisive limitations here are the uncontrolled optimizer comparison and absence of matched epoch-budget results. Section 4.3 also repeats a paragraph referring to Figure 2; use its subsequent Figure 3 comparison for the CNN finding.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD under tuning conditions.
Fixed epoch-budget comparisons; language models; whether longer training, warmup, normalization or regularization changes remove a large-batch penalty.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: 3-layer stacked LSTM on sequential MNIST (7 × 7) classification task
rows.size_stated: Each LSTM has 10 hidden units; three LSTM layers and a fully-connected layer.
rows.operation_detail: Block-diagonal Hessian-free optimization with large mini-batches; test accuracy compared with Adam at any mini-batch size.
rows.value: requires far fewer updates to achieve lower training loss and better test accuracy than Adam with any mini-batch size
rows.note: The text reports the comparison in aggregate across the two stated curvature mini-batch sizes; it does not give numeric test-accuracy values. It does not hold epoch budget fixed.
rows.check: This is a proposed-optimizer performance comparison, not a controlled test of V5. Large-batch block-diagonal HF achieves better test accuracy than the tested Adam settings, but optimizer and training exposure are not held fixed. Replace 'any mini-batch size' with 'the tested mini-batch sizes, 100 and 6000'; Figure 2 shows only those Adam settings.

rows.subject: simplified residual CNN
rows.size_stated: One convolutional layer (16 × 32 × 32), three residual blocks, and a fully-connected layer; batch normalization omitted.
rows.operation_detail: Block-diagonal Hessian-free optimization with large mini-batches; test accuracy compared with Adam using small mini-batches.

conditions.value: Polyak averaging with exponential decay rate 0.99

rows.value: comparable test accuracy to Adam with small ones
rows.note: The text states this comparison without numeric accuracy values. It does not hold epoch budget fixed.
rows.check: Comparable accuracy between large-batch block-diagonal HF and small-batch Adam does not determine the fixed-epoch batch-size effect. The optimizer changes, and the shared 1000-epoch ceiling permits different stopping epochs. Specify Adam batch 256 as the small-batch baseline. The qualitative value is supported, but 'partial' is not a warranted state for V5.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
